chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I command the servant girl to look whether dawn has risen or not; if she says it has not risen, I eat. Then I look and find that it has risen by the time she looked.' He said: 'You complete your day and you also make up for it (perform qada). Is it not that if you were the one who looked, there would not be any qada upon you?'

key_terms.اَلْفَجْرُ: dawn (the time for Fajr prayer and fasting begins)
key_terms.طَلَعَ: rose/appeared (referring to the emergence of dawn)
key_terms.قَضَاءُ: make-up fast (performing a missed fast at a later time)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting if a servant mistakenly tells you dawn hasn't risen?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *ghalat* (error) in fasting, distinguishing between negligence and genuine mistake based on the observer's direct involvement. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that delegating the task to a servant introduces a layer of reliance that, if mistaken, requires both *qada* (make-up) and *kaffarah* (expiation) or full completion, whereas self-verification mitigates the penalty. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on personal diligence (*ijtihad*) in determining the precise onset of *Fajr al-Sadiq*.
